conversation.content:
Hi there. I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—I specialize in the emotional well-being of new mothers. I’ll be guiding you through a brief screening called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply a set of ten questions that help us understand how you’ve been feeling during the past seven days so we can make sure you’re getting the support you deserve. Everything you share stays between us, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. When you’re ready, we’ll go through the questions one by one; each should only take a moment. Let’s start gently:  

Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[soft sigh, eyes drop to the floor]  
I’ve laughed a little—maybe once when my husband sent a silly meme—but mostly it feels forced. Things that used to crack me up just slide past me now. It’s like the lightness is stuck behind a fog.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

[slow head-shake]  
Not really. I can manage a small chuckle if someone tries hard to be funny, but it fades fast. Most of the time nothing feels funny at all.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[sighs, twisting the edge of my robe]  
Sometimes I’ll think “oh, it might be nice to take the baby for a walk,” but when the time comes I don’t really feel excited. Even coffee with my best friend sounded fun on the calendar, but an hour before I just wanted to stay in bed.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[quietly, eyes welling]  
All the time. If the baby spits up more than usual, I’m sure I ate something wrong. When he wouldn’t nap yesterday I kept thinking, “I’m failing him—other moms know how to do this.” I know in my head it’s not all my fault, but the guilt just barges in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

[wrings hands]  
Yeah… pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly picture him not breathing in the bassinet, or worry that the stroller will roll into traffic. Nothing sets it off, but once the thought comes it keeps looping until I check on him—again.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

[voice trembles]  
A few times. Like last night, I was rocking the baby and my heart just started racing—I felt like I couldn’t catch my breath. Nothing was wrong, but for a minute I thought I might pass out. It passed after I put him down and stepped outside, but it was scary.
Things have been getting on top of me

[exhales shakily]  
Yes… most days. The dishes pile up, I can’t remember if I ate, and every tiny task feels like a mountain. I usually push through for the baby, but I end up crying once or twice a week when it all feels too heavy.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

[eyes rimmed with tiredness]  
Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my brain keeps listing everything I might have messed up that day. It takes me forever to drift off, and when I finally do I wake up with a jolt thinking I heard the baby cry—even if he’s still asleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

[Voice drops, almost a whisper]  
Most of the day, almost every day. It’s like there’s this gray cloud parked over me. I can still smile for the baby, but as soon as he’s settled the heaviness settles right back in.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[nods slowly, pressing a tissue to her eyes]  
Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Once when my mom asked how I was doing, and once after a diaper change that took forever. The tears just came and I couldn’t stop them, even though part of me felt silly for crying over something so small.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[voice cracks, fingers tighten around the tissue]  
A couple of times… just fleeting. Like when I’m rocking him at 3 a.m. and everything feels hopeless, I’ll think, “What if I just disappeared?” I don’t have a plan or anything, and I’d never leave my baby, but the thought flashes in and scares me.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms endorsed (10/10 items):
- Anhedonia, pervasive low mood, daily tearfulness  
- Marked loss of enjoyment (even anticipated activities)  
- Excessive inappropriate guilt and self-blame regarding infant care  
- Persistent intrusive worries (SIDs, safety) and panic-like episodes  
- Overwhelm with routine tasks; frequent crying spells (≥2×/wk)  
- Initial and maintenance insomnia linked to ruminative worry  
- Passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent (“What if I just disappeared?”)

Pattern: Symptoms present most of the day, nearly every day, for ≥2 weeks; cause functional impairment (unable to complete basic tasks, avoiding outings).  
Risk factors: Primiparity, sleep deprivation, absence of perceived social support, passive SI.  
Safety: Denies intent or plan; nevertheless flagged for immediate follow-up.

Screening impression: High clinical likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; rule-out postpartum anxiety disorder.  
Recommendation: Urgent referral to obstetric/postpartum mental-health specialist for comprehensive evaluation and safety planning.
